Harbour Vale School -
Harbour Vale School provides a friendly, safe and welcoming environment.
Our curriculum is designed to enable our students to achieve their full potential.
We provide students with the necessary skills and abilities to be successful members of society.
We treat every student as an individual with their own wants, needs, gifts and talents.
Welcome to Harbour Vale School
Harbour Vale School, a pupil referral unit and academy in North Dorset, empowers every young person who joins us to believe, achieve and succeed: we meet them where they are with a therapeutic thinking approach and a holistic education that heals gaps, builds resilience, respect and responsibility, and restores opportunities. Through tailored academic and pastoral support, practical life skills and community partnership, we shape confident, compassionate and capable young people ready to re-engage with mainstream education, training or work and become valued members of society.

Personal Development
Personal Development at Harbour Vale
At Harbour Vale we believe in facilitating the holistic development of all our students by ensuring they can make positive choices which will, in turn, provide them with the skills to create a healthy, productive and positive future.
Our personal development curriculum offers unique learning experiences which provide students with enriched cultural capital. By offering a diverse set of experiences, we help to prepare students for the culturally diverse nature of the society in which we live. We deliver a curriculum designed to ensure students are resilient, respectful, and responsible.
Our Personal Development curriculum has the following aims:
PSHE (Personal, Social, Health and Economic education) including RSE (Relationships and Sex Education) and SEMH (Social, Emotional, and Mental Health) as well as Citizenship provide the backbone to our Personal Development curriculum. Careers Education also plays an important role in providing experiences for the personal development of our students. We have an extensive trips and visits programme which supports these aims, and further intervention and enrichment activities such as fitness, variety of sports, child development, hairdressing, cooking, business studies and community activities provide a huge range of opportunities for students to excel at both an individual and community level.

Music
Intent
At Harbour Vale School, we believe that all pupils should have opportunities to engage with music, regardless of their previous experiences, confidence levels or educational backgrounds. Our music provision is designed to support personal development, wellbeing, self-expression and creativity while fostering confidence, resilience and aspiration.
We provide meaningful opportunities for pupils to explore and develop musical skills through enrichment activities and informal learning experiences. Our approach is particularly beneficial for pupils with SEND and those who may have experienced barriers to learning in mainstream settings, as music provides an alternative means of communication, achievement and emotional expression.
The sequencing of our provision focuses on developing engagement and confidence first, before introducing more complex musical skills and experiences helping them discover personal interests, talents and potential future pathways within music and the creative industries.
Implementation
Music is delivered through enrichment opportunities and instrument tuition available during social times and through a weekly enrichment programme. Pupils can access and learn a range of instruments, including ukuleles, keyboards and guitars, in a supportive and informal environment.
Practitioners provide opportunities for pupils to develop fundamental musical skills such as rhythm, timing, listening, coordination and performance. Learning is practical and highly personalised, allowing pupils to progress at a pace appropriate to their individual needs and interests.
Where appropriate, pupils are supported to build their knowledge and confidence over time through repeated practice, performance opportunities and exposure to different musical genres and techniques. Partnerships with external providers, including Dorset Music Service, help to broaden experiences and provide access to specialist expertise and resources.
Impact
The impact of our music provision is demonstrated through increased pupil engagement, confidence, wellbeing and willingness to participate in new experiences. Pupils develop practical musical skills, improve their ability to work collaboratively and gain confidence in performing and expressing themselves creatively.
Assessment is primarily based on participation, skill development, personal progress and engagement with musical activities. Staff monitor pupils’ growing confidence, independence and musical competence through observation and discussion.
As opportunities continue to develop, we aim to expand progression routes into accredited learning, performance opportunities and wider musical experiences, ensuring that pupils leave Harbour Vale with positive experiences of music and an appreciation of its value in supporting wellbeing and lifelong learning.

Art
Intent
It is our intention at Harbour Vale School to develop curious creativity, understanding, progression and positivity through sequenced, relevant and engaging lessons. We deliver an adaptive and research based art curriculum centred around foundation art skills, which students employ to explore and further develop independent and collaborative creative experience. Our curriculum is designed to scaffold individual and shared knowledge to encourage work that is developed from core knowledge, fulfils creative intention/s and thoroughly investigates, deepens and develops visual language. HVS art students develop their knowledge of art, artists and cultures to inspire and enrich their own and others’ creative growth and cultural capital. Traditional media and techniques are complemented by contemporary thought and practice.
Our students learn to develop critical thinking skills, creative problem solving and to scaffold confidence in articulating their responses and ideas visually, verbally and in written forms.
The Formal Elements form a central spine for all learning, responses and success. Students have the opportunity to explore a wide range of traditional and contemporary media both in 2D and 3D and where possible will engage in art activities in the wider community. We provide a creative and community based environment allowing students of all abilities and stages to enhance and build upon prior knowledge in a safe, challenging and aspirational environment based on mutual respect and British Values. A relational and therapeutic approach is embedded to facilitate the improvement of key academic and personal skills to aspire for a future beyond HVS.
Implementation
To support and recognise creative achievement at HVS we offer Arts Award and GCSE.
It is our intention that every student at Harbour Vale School will work towards Arts Award ‘Discover’ and ‘Explore’ certification. This applies to onsite and Pathways students and short and long term placements.
All students will access art lessons at KS3 and have the choice to study GCSE Art and Design at KS4.
KS3 Art and Design: Years 7/8/9
KS4 Art and Design: Years 10/11
GCSE Art and Design is split into two components:
C1 and C2 is Externally Moderated.
At HVS, our commitment to all students’ creative development is underpinned by Arts Award.
All KS4 Students, whether onsite or on our pathways programme will follow the Art Award Discover and in some cases Explore certification, thereby receiving recognition of their engagement and celebrating success.
Impact
All students in art at HVS are encouraged and challenged to explore their full creative potential no matter their starting point. Student progress will be measured through regular portfolio, creative outcomes and assessment as they move through their learning pathway. Students will be aware of and be able to create in a wide range of media and techniques. Students will be able to engage, recognise and talk about art with increasing confidence and will develop a wider appreciation of art and culture from different genres and cultures from around the world (Cultural Capital). The ability to present work both physically and verbally will be evident and students will be able to articulate ideas and artwork with increasing levels of vocabulary and oracy.
Students will be able to measure success through common assessment language (assessment objectives and taxonomy) based on the Formal Elements and around assessment criteria (EDEXCEL/Pearson and Arts Award/Trinity College/Discover/Explore) Students will acquire demonstrably transferable skills that they can transfer to future learning at Post 16 ensuring that they are equipped to contribute positively to their communities, future workplace and career/s.
Partnerships and wider creative collaborations:
To enhance school based art and design provision, we are committed to engaging and building creative partnerships to support creative progression and cultural capital.
Oliver’s Cafe: in Sherborne works with us closely to provide local community art engagement opportunities. Window designs designed and made by HVS art students have this year won two competitions through The Sherborne Chamber of Commerce and British Legion.
AUB – Arts University Bournemouth: Annual Being a Boy Creative Workshops and AUB/HVS creative partnership.
Hauser and Wirth International Art Gallery/Bruton: Art based trips and partnership to enrich wider appreciation and knowledge.
Arts Award: We are a recognised Arts Award Centre. Arts Award is affiliated to Trinity College and Arts Council England.
GCSE: Recognised Edexcel GCSE centre.
We are proud of our local and national associations with the above institutions and are committed in working towards rapidly developing further art opportunities.

Citizenship
Harbour Vale School’s aim throughout the GCSE Citizenship course is to engage pupils in the local and global world; to help them consider their role as global citizens and to think critically but proactively about a politicised environment.
The course encourages students to play an active part in public and democratic life as informed and active citizens. The Edexcel Citizenship Studies GCSE allows for the group or individual undertaking of citizenship action and for students to develop the ability to analyse and comment on four key themes.
Students build on Key Stage 3 knowledge and understanding and are introduced to core concepts and how citizenship impacts on their lives before developing this with the introduction of theory and the ‘bigger picture’ as they progress through the course. The course also focuses on the importance of active citizenship so students can engage with topics close to their hearts while they develop skills in research and investigation, problem solving, advocacy and campaigning. Citizenship Studies at GCSE reflects current issues, questions and debates; and therefore, students develop knowledge and understanding of the role of citizenship in relation to the political and democratic issues and discourse that impacts on modern society. Throughout the course, students are supported to become confident public speakers who advocate on behalf of others. The Citizenship Course also works on a Cross curricular level by focusing on key areas such as Literacy, comparing sources and analysing text, deconstructing political vocabulary and debating.
The aims and objectives of Citizenship Studies are to enable students to know and understand what democracy is, how parliamentary democracy operates within the constituent parts of the UK, how government works and how democratic and nondemocratic systems of government are different beyond the UK; know and understand the relationship between the state and citizens, the rights, responsibilities and duties of citizens living and working in the UK and how people participate in democracy , know and understand the role of the law in society, how laws are shaped and enforced and how the justice system works in England and Wales, know and understand how taxes are raised and spent by governments, and how national economic and financial policies and decisions relate to individuals, use and apply knowledge and understanding of key citizenship ideas and concepts, including democracy, government, justice, equality, rights, responsibilities, participation, community, identity and diversity, to think deeply and critically about a wide range of political, social, economic and ethical issues and questions facing society in local to global contexts, use and apply knowledge and understanding as they formulate citizenship enquiries, explore and research citizenship issues and actions, analyse and evaluate information and interpret sources of evidence.
A) Living together in the UK – Students are introduced to the idea that the UK is a diverse society of many different communities and groups who live together. They explore the nature of identity and multiple identities as well as how and why communities are changing. They consider the democratic rights, freedoms and values that we share, including human rights and the challenge of balancing competing rights. Opportunities for developing citizenship skills include: to debate and explore identities, rights, values and democracy, and to gain a practical understanding of being an active citizen through contributing to local democracy and taking citizenship action to resolve problems, tackle inequality and improve justice.
B) Democracy at work in the UK – Students explore the idea of representative, parliamentary democracy in the UK including the voting and electoral system, the roles and responsibilities of MPs and how government is organised and kept in check. They will also consider the role of parliament in making and shaping law; the government’s role in managing public money; and how power is organised across the constituent parts of the UK. Opportunities for developing citizenship skills and taking action include participation in decision making forums and ‘mock’ or real school elections, researching and debating the effectiveness of democracy in the UK, the extension of voting rights to 16- and 17-year-olds or further devolution of power versus independence for Scotland, Northern Ireland and Wales.
C) Law and Justice – Students explore why we need laws and how law affects us in our everyday lives. They consider how the justice system in England and Wales works in practice including the roles and power of the police and the courts. They also learn about the distinctive features of the criminal, civil and youth justice systems and some of the different approaches to settling disputes, addressing inequality, changing behaviour and tackling crime in society. Opportunities for developing citizenship skills and taking action include investigating different legal cases, participation in ‘mock’ trials and sentencing decision-making activities, debating whether it is ever right to break the law or whether the justice system treats everyone fairly. Students could undertake citizenship action or campaigns to address inequality or an injustice.
D) Power and Influence – In this section students revisit key ideas about democracy, rights and responsibilities in Themes A–C as they explore ideas about power. They consider power in relation to the ways in which citizens, governments and the media exercise power and influence in a range of local to global situations. They contrast representative democracy in the UK with a non-democratic political system and the limits this places on the rights and freedoms of citizens. Opportunities to develop citizenship skills include examining ways in which citizens co-operate to try and improve society and democracy through different kinds of political and citizen actions; practical experiences of taking citizenship action themselves to address issues; debating the relationship of the UK with Europe; and investigating global issues and problems facing society from the environment to humanitarian and conflict situations.
E) Taking Citizenship Action – Citizenship action may be defined as a planned course of informed action to address a citizenship issue or question of concern and aimed at delivering a benefit or change for a particular community or wider society. Taking citizenship action in a real out-of-classroom context allows students to apply citizenship knowledge, understanding and skills, and to gain different citizenship insights and appreciate different perspectives on how we live together and make decisions in society. It requires them to practise a range of citizenship skills including research and enquiry, interpretation of evidence, including primary and secondary sources, planning, collaboration, problem solving, advocacy, campaigning and evaluation.
Harbour Vale School’s Citizenship curriculum is delivered with the aim to ensure that students gain the powerful knowledge they need to be active and informed citizens. We strive to provide students with safe spaces within which to explore and develop their ideas about Citizenship issues, facilitated by trusted adults who understand our community and the individual histories of the students in the class. This gives our students the opportunity to explore contested issues in a safe space, facilitated by teachers who know them and their personal history well and who can respond to individual and community contexts sensitively. This will necessarily involve discussing controversial questions and challenging misconceptions that may be widespread among our students.
Assessment is conducted through formative assessment and the use of targeted questions within each lesson to ensure key concepts have been grasped. In addition, retrieval practice takes place at the start of each lesson to ensure that key knowledge is retained in students’ long-term memory, and key questions are planned to ensure students’ progress to the next topic only when understanding of foundation topics is secure. Lesson resources are shared amongst teaching staff to maintain consistency, based on the sequential lesson planning document. Students are made aware of connections to career options such as public and emergency services, third sector work, being a local councillor or other elected representative, and working within the justice system.
Formative assessment activities are built into every Citizenship lesson delivered at Harbour Vale School and through other subject curricula. This is done through retrieval quizzing of previously taught material, targeted questions that check for understanding of foundational concepts, and discussion tasks which enable teachers to identify misconceptions and address them in the moment they are noticed.
For those students studying the GCSE Citizenship Studies course, there are many qualitative indicators that will help us assess the extent to which our intent has been delivered alongside the examination at the end of Key stage 4. Key signs would be that a high proportion of student’s volunteer within school and in the wider community, that they ask questions of their tutors and subject teachers that indicate an engagement with current affairs, and express positions in favour of human rights and standing up to injustice and disadvantage.
We will know that our students have developed a true love of Citizenship if they demonstrate responsible behaviour as up standers within and beyond school as a result of their powerful knowledge gained through Citizenship. This can be tracked through behaviour data, reports on trends in behaviours such as bullying and discrimination in staff meetings, and feedback from our Pupil Welfare Officer about student interaction with police and the justice system. If our intent has been successful and students love the subject, they will engage in discussion with parents, carers and friends about what they see in the media; we would also expect that parents and carers will report on consultation evenings that students are eager to discuss their interest in Citizenship issues and political events such as elections and are keen to complete volunteer work. In the longer term we would expect to see students applying for courses and choosing careers in the public services and third sector, politics, law and finance, based on the knowledge and understanding gained during their time studying Citizenship at Harbour Vale School.

Computing
KS3 COMPUTING:
Intent:
The Harbour Vale School KS3 Computing Curriculum includes formal teaching throughout a wide range of subject areas. Students will learn a wide range of problem-solving skills, programming skills, collaboration, creativity and interest for pursuing a future career in the subject. All skills are taught in a sequential manner to support independence in assessments. The projects and topics are developed to ensure that each year students embed and build upon previous knowledge and skills. The KS3 Computing Curriculum allows students to put into practice what they learn to further embed knowledge. Learners will use a range of industry led software and hardware to enable them to flourish in a world dominated by digital technology and opportunities. Our intent is underpinned by a culture of high aspirations and each student believing that by working hard they can achieve their very best. In every topic, links to careers and the world of work are made. The curriculum is regularly monitored and adapted to suit the needs of all our learners.
Implementation:
Harbour Vale School staff work collaboratively to ensure that all students can access the KS3 Computing curriculum, using their expertise to differentiate lessons accordingly. All skills are sequenced from year 7 to 9 to ensure students are progressing each year and they can continuously retrieve information from each project. High quality questioning and resources are used during practical lessons and theory lessons.
Assessments and quality feedback are used at the end of each topic to inform students of their progress and achievements, this will allow students to progress to the next level with skills and knowledge. Students will learn the fundamentals of design, development and testing. This will provide learners with skills in E-Safety, Social media, Computer Systems, Programming, project management and Spreadsheets.
Impact:
Harbour Vale school staff and students recognise that we are living in an era dominated by digital technology, and this is why computing is such a needed subject within schools. Our school encourages discussions between staff and pupils to help the children best understand their progress and their next steps. We measure the impact of our curriculum through such methods as Pupil discussions and interviewing the pupils about their learning (pupil voice), Pupil assessment and feedback on content creation, Moderation staff meetings with opportunities for dialogue between teachers, Pupil self-reflection, A reflection on standards achieved against the planned outcomes (progression/what to observe in learning), Learning walks and reflective staff feedback and Formative and summative approaches. Here at Harbour Vale School, we wish that all of our students gain an understanding of Computing and feel confident in using technology safely and securely as part of their daily lives.

KS4 COMPUTING:
Intent:
The Harbour Vale School KS4 Computing curriculum has been designed to ensure all learners are able to achieve the highest standards and outcomes following the specification from Pearson. Essential Digital Skills is learner focused and has been developed to ensure students learn computational thinking skills, conceptual learning and understanding. Students will be able to think creatively, logically and critically while understanding the components that make up digital systems and valuable thinking and programming skills that are required in the modern workplace. Our assessment structure allows learners to build on what they learn while continuously developing industry required skills. Upon completion of the course, students will possess the key elements required to enter jobs in the Computing sector such as problem solving, analytical skills and a wide computing background.
Implementation:
Pearson’s Essential Digital skills course can be assessed at 2 levels, these are Entry level and Level 1; These levels consist of three externally set and internally marked assessments. They are available as on-demand assessments. The content areas cover Using Devices and Handling Information, Creating and Editing, Communicating, Transacting and Being Safe and Responsible Online. Summative assessment criteria are used to ensure all students can achieve and exceed desired outcomes during the course. Practical lessons alongside theory lessons are used for each topic alongside the end of unit tests. An effective assessment process allows learners and staff to identify areas for improvements.
Impact
Students recognise we are living in an era dominated by digital technology, and this is why Computing is such a needed subject within schools. Our school encourages discussions between staff and pupils to help the children best understand their progress and their next steps. We measure the impact of our curriculum through such methods as Pupil discussions and interviewing the pupils about their learning (pupil voice), Pupil assessment and feedback on content creation, Moderation staff meetings with opportunities for dialogue between teachers, Pupil self-reflection, A reflection on standards achieved against the planned outcomes (progression/what to observe in learning), Learning walks and reflective staff feedback and Formative and summative approaches. Here at Harbour Vale School, we wish that all our students gain an understanding of Computing and feel confident in using technology safely and securely as part of their daily lives, making clear links to how this links to their post 16 provision and future careers.

Maths
Intent The intent of our mathematics curriculum is to provide students with a foundation for understanding number, reasoning, thinking logically and problem solving with resilience so that they are fully prepared for the future. It is essential that these keystones of Mathematics are embedded throughout all strands of the National Curriculum. It is also intended that all students, regardless of their starting point, will maximise their academic achievement and leave Harbour Vale School with an appreciation and enthusiasm for Maths, resulting in a lifelong positive relationship with number. We ensure that we deliver a high quality maths curriculum that is both challenging and enjoyable. We want students to make rich connections across mathematical ideas to develop fluency, mathematical reasoning and competence in solving increasingly sophisticated problems. We intend for our students to be able to apply their mathematical knowledge to science and other subjects. We want them to know that maths is essential to everyday life, careers and that our students are confident mathematicians who are not afraid to take risks. Fully develop independent learners with inquisitive minds who have secure mathematical skills and an interest in self-improvement and feel confident when leaving Habour Vale School and the career paths that they pursue.
Implementation Our implementation is developed through secure understanding of the curriculum and subject area. Long term planning follows the National Curriculum. Short term planning is based on individual student need and planning from feeder schools. By using a variety of resources we provide a bespoke teaching and learning experience that is designed to interest, inform and inspire our students. Using prior knowledge as a starting point for all future planning and teaching, we plan lessons which are required for all students to make good progress. Lessons are engaging and follow a cycle of planning, to ensure that we can evidence progress over short and long periods of time. Lessons are designed to provide students with the scaffolding required to access the learning at all levels. Students are invested in their learning and are making a positive contribution to their lessons. Assessment informs the teaching and learning sequence, and students work on the objectives they are assessed as being at. Students who not making the required progress are given extra support through additional lessons and support in class in order to meet our INTENT of developing students academically. Feedback is given on student’s learning in line with our feedback policy. Formative assessment within every lesson helps teachers to identify the students who need more support to achieve the intended outcome and who are ready for greater stretch and challenge through planned questioning or additional activities. In order to support teacher judgments, students are assessed using current and reliable tests in line with the national curriculum for maths. Analysis of any tests that the students complete is undertaken and fed into future planning. Summative assessments are completed at the end of the academic year and help influence the overall judgement reported to parents in the end of year report. Working with SLT, key data is analysed and regular feedback is provided and discussed at pupil progress meetings to inform progress and future actions.
Impact When leaving Harbour Vale School students will demonstrate quick recall of facts and procedures as well as have the flexibility and fluidity to move between different contexts and representations of mathematics. They will have the ability to recognise relationships and make connections in mathematics. Students will show a high level of pride in the presentation and understanding of the work. Students will show confidence in believing that they will achieve. Students are prepared for the world of work, college, training or apprenticeships with high aspirations and ambitions.

Physical Education
Intent
At Harbour Vale School, our Physical Education curriculum is designed to meet the diverse and often complex needs of our pupils through a therapeutic, inclusive and high-quality approach. We recognise that physical activity is not only important for physical health but also plays a vital role in supporting emotional wellbeing, personal development and positive mental health.
Our curriculum aims to provide all pupils with access to a broad and engaging range of physical activities, enabling them to develop confidence, competence and enjoyment in movement. Through participation in sport, fitness and outdoor learning experiences, pupils develop resilience, self-awareness and a positive sense of identity. The curriculum is carefully designed to support pupils in building lifelong habits that promote healthy lifestyles while developing key personal qualities such as teamwork, communication, leadership and emotional literacy.
The curriculum is sequenced to ensure pupils first develop confidence and engagement before progressing towards greater independence, skill acquisition and participation in increasingly challenging physical activities. Activities are adapted and personalised to ensure all learners, including those with SEND and social, emotional and mental health needs, can experience success and make meaningful progress.
Implementation
Physical Education is delivered through a diverse programme of practical activities across Key Stages 3 and 4, providing pupils with opportunities to experience a wide variety of sporting, fitness and outdoor learning environments.
These opportunities include:
Pupils are also offered opportunities to represent Harbour Vale through participation in the school football team, where they can engage in regular training sessions, friendly fixtures and inclusive competitive events.
Lessons are carefully scaffolded to support individual needs and ensure progression over time. Practitioners use modelling, coaching, reflection and personalised targets to build pupils’ confidence and competence. Opportunities for literacy, numeracy, oracy, careers education and personal development are embedded throughout the curriculum. Pupils are encouraged to take ownership of their learning through planning, self-evaluation and peer coaching activities, helping them to develop independence and transferable life skills.
For pupils with a particular interest in sport and fitness, opportunities are available to study Occupational Studies qualifications focused on planning and participating in fitness and sporting activities, providing valuable vocational learning experiences and potential progression pathways.
Impact
The impact of the Physical Education curriculum is evident through pupils’ increased participation, confidence and engagement in physical activity. Pupils develop the knowledge, skills and motivation required to lead active and healthy lifestyles both during and beyond their time at Harbour Vale.
Through regular participation, pupils demonstrate improved physical competence, emotional regulation, resilience and social skills. They become more confident working collaboratively, managing challenges and reflecting on their own progress. Many pupils develop a greater understanding of the relationship between physical activity, mental wellbeing and overall health.
Assessment is ongoing and focuses on both physical development and personal progress. Staff monitor pupils’ engagement, skill acquisition, fitness levels, teamwork, leadership and personal development through observation, discussion and practical performance.
The curriculum contributes significantly to Harbour Vale’s culture of wellbeing, inclusion, aspiration and personal growth, ensuring pupils leave with the confidence and skills to participate safely and independently in physical activity throughout their lives.

Science
KS3
Intent
It is our intention at Harbour Vale school to develop trust, understanding and positivity through well planned, sequenced and engaging lessons. Our aim is to develop a curriculum which shows how science applies to the world in which we live, inspiring students to critically think about science and develop skills which can apply across the curriculum.
We aim to provide an environment allowing students of all abilities to enhance and build upon their prior knowledge in science, improving key academic and personal skills in order to have aspirations for the future beyond Harbour Vale School.
Implementation
In key stage 3 science students learn a combination of Biology, Chemistry and Physics knowledge, utilising and building upon their previous learning and skills from years 7 through to year 9.
Due to the differing nature of their placements, educational backgrounds and the time of year of which pupils arrive at Harbour Vale School; each child will start at the most appropriate step in the learning journey to give them the best possible chance of success in their future learning.
Students will be taught how to work safely, identify equipment and how to use the correct scientific method. They will explore scientific careers through discussion. Student’s knowledge and understanding is checked regularly alongside structured teacher feedback allowing students to reflect, grow and deepen their understanding in a safe and supportive environment.
Impact
At Harbour Vale School we endeavour to ensure that all students reach their full potential in science, no matter their starting point. Student progress will be measured through regular assessments as they move through their learning journeys.
Students will be able to work scientifically, think and challenge as a scientist and be able to reason and evaluate the world around them.
We aim to educate students academically and emotionally so they can prepare themselves for their next steps as they will know the options available to them regarding study, careers and apprenticeships; aspiring them to study science in the future.
Science KS3 Learning Journey
Year 10 GCSE AQA Combined Science: Synergy
Intent
The Year 10 curriculum provides an ambitious and inclusive science education that develops pupils’ knowledge, practical skills and scientific thinking. Pupils are introduced to key concepts across Biology, Chemistry and Physics, while developing their ability to analyse data, evaluate evidence and apply scientific knowledge. Learning is carefully sequenced to build understanding over time, with adaptive teaching and appropriate challenge ensuring all learners, including those with SEND, can access and succeed in the curriculum.
Implementation
The curriculum is delivered through carefully planned units that introduce new scientific concepts and practical skills. Teachers use retrieval practice, questioning and regular assessment to reinforce learning and address misconceptions. Scientific vocabulary and literacy are explicitly taught throughout. Oracy strategies are used to develop pupils’ confidence in discussing scientific ideas, explaining concepts and justifying their thinking, while providing teachers with opportunities to assess understanding and address misconceptions. Pupils complete the required practical activities, developing their skills in planning, conducting, analysing and evaluating investigations. Across the course, pupils gain experience of all 21 required practical activities that support understanding of key scientific concepts and prepare them for examination questions.
Impact
Pupils develop secure foundational knowledge and practical skills across all science disciplines. Regular assessments, including verbal responses and scientific discussions, demonstrate increasing confidence in scientific enquiry, data analysis and extended scientific writing. Pupils are able to apply their knowledge to unfamiliar contexts and are well prepared for the more examination-focused demands of Year 11.
Year 11 GCSE AQA Combined Science: Synergy
Intent
The Year 11 curriculum builds upon pupils’ scientific knowledge and focuses on securing long-term retention, developing examination confidence and preparing pupils for GCSE success. Pupils refine their understanding of key concepts across Biology, Chemistry and Physics while strengthening their ability to apply knowledge, interpret data and answer examination-style questions. Adaptive teaching and targeted intervention ensure all learners, including those with SEND, are supported to achieve their potential.
Implementation
The curriculum is delivered through a combination of final content delivery, systematic revision and examination preparation. Teachers use retrieval practice, low-stakes testing and regular examination questions to strengthen memory and address gaps in learning. Oracy is embedded through structured scientific discussions, questioning and verbal explanations, enabling pupils to articulate their understanding while providing teachers with ongoing opportunities for formative assessment. The 21 required practical activities are revisited through practical work, recall activities and examination questions to ensure pupils understand the methods, variables, data analysis and evaluation skills required for assessment. Pupils complete regular topic tests, mock examinations and structured revision activities in preparation for the four AQA Combined Science: Synergy GCSE examination papers.
Impact
Pupils demonstrate strong retention of scientific knowledge and are able to confidently apply their understanding to a range of examination contexts. Assessment outcomes, including verbal questioning, mock examinations and GCSE results, show that pupils are prepared for the demands of the four final examination papers. Pupils leave the course with the scientific knowledge, practical understanding and examination skills needed for further study and future success.

Esports
Intent:
The Esports curriculum provides structured, purposeful learning through a highly engaging and relevant subject area that supports re‑engagement with education. Students are taught a broad range of transferable skills including teamwork, communication, strategic thinking, problem solving, leadership, resilience and digital literacy. Learning is carefully sequenced to build confidence, independence and positive learning behaviours over time, enabling students to experience success and take pride in their achievements.
The curriculum is designed to meet the diverse needs of learners within a Pupil Referral Unit, using esports as a motivating context to develop social skills, emotional regulation, and self‑discipline alongside technical knowledge. Students explore both competitive and non‑competitive roles within esports, including event management, content creation, analysis, health and wellbeing, and digital citizenship, helping them to recognise their strengths and interests.
Projects are practical and applied, allowing students to put learning into action and embed knowledge through real‑world scenarios. Industry‑relevant software, hardware and current practices are used to ensure learning is meaningful and aspirational, while also promoting safe, responsible and balanced use of technology.
Our intent is underpinned by high expectations, inclusivity and a strong belief that every student can succeed. Clear links are made to careers, qualifications, and pathways into further education, training and employment. The curriculum is regularly reviewed and adapted to ensure it remains responsive to students’ needs, supports positive outcomes, and prepares learners for life beyond School.
Implementation:
The Esports curriculum is delivered through a structured and flexible approach that supports engagement, positive behaviour and progression. Learning is organised into clearly sequenced units, with a strong emphasis on practical application, vocational relevance and skill development.
Students complete two substantial coursework units across the course. These units are carefully designed to allow learners to demonstrate knowledge, creativity and independence while working towards a meaningful final outcome. Coursework tasks are broken down into manageable stages, with clear success criteria and regular opportunities for review and improvement. This approach supports learners with varying needs and promotes resilience, organisation and ownership of learning.
Teaching incorporates a balance of theoretical understanding and practical activity, including team-based projects, esports match analysis, event organisation, content creation and reflection on roles within the esports industry. Industry-relevant software and hardware are used wherever possible to ensure authenticity and engagement.
Formative assessment is embedded throughout every lesson and unit. This includes questioning, discussion, observation of practical tasks, peer and self-assessment, feedback against success criteria, and reflection activities. Formative assessment is used to identify misconceptions, adapt teaching, and provide timely, supportive feedback that helps students build confidence and make progress.
Summative assessment takes place at key points within each unit, including the completion of coursework components, end-of-unit assessments, and final project submissions. Summative tasks are designed to assess both subject knowledge and transferable skills such as teamwork, communication, planning and problem solving. Assessment outcomes are used to inform next steps, celebrate achievement, and support progression pathways.
Assessment methods are adapted where appropriate to meet individual needs, ensuring that all learners can access the curriculum and demonstrate success. Progress is regularly reviewed, and the curriculum is adjusted to ensure it remains responsive, inclusive and ambitious for every student.
Impact:
The Esports curriculum has a positive impact on student engagement, attendance and attitudes to learning within the Pupil Referral Unit. By using a highly relevant and motivating subject, students are re‑engaged with education and demonstrate increased confidence, improved behaviour for learning, and a willingness to take part in structured activities.
Students make measurable progress in both subject‑specific knowledge and transferable life skills, including communication, teamwork, leadership, resilience, problem solving and self‑reflection. The completion of two coursework units enables learners to experience success, develop a sense of achievement and take pride in producing meaningful, high‑quality work.
Regular formative and summative assessment shows that students are able to recall knowledge, apply skills independently and build on prior learning over time. Learners develop a clearer understanding of expectations, are better able to regulate their behaviour, and demonstrate improved focus, perseverance and collaboration.
The curriculum supports successful progression by increasing awareness of career pathways, further education and training opportunities within and beyond the esports industry. Students leave the provision with improved digital literacy, employability skills and a more positive outlook on their own potential. Overall, the impact of the Esports curriculum is seen in improved engagement, personal development, and readiness for the next stage of education, employment or training.

Academy Committees
The Academy Committee (AC) supports the Trustees in providing effective oversight of Harbour Vale Academy. Acting as the Board’s eyes and ears at a local level, the Committee helps ensure that the school continues to provide the highest standards of education, care and support for its students.
While key operational services such as Finance, Human Resources, Estates and IT are managed centrally by the SAST team, the Academy Committee focuses on matters that directly impact students and school life.

The Academy Committee includes parent and staff representatives, alongside members appointed by the Trustees for their skills, knowledge and experience. The Headteacher serves as an ex officio member.
Academy Committee members are appointed for a four-year term and may be reappointed for further terms.
The Committee meets three times a year, once at the beginning of each full term. An additional meeting is held during the autumn term to review published examination outcomes and student performance data.

Intent
Harbour Vale School is a pupil referral unit located in a residential area of Sherborne, North Dorset. We provide a relational, inclusive and therapeutic learning environment for pupils who are unable to access or sustain engagement in mainstream education, or who require targeted intervention to support reintegration.
Our core purpose is for every student to BELIEVE, ACHIEVE, SUCCEED. We are committed to developing the whole child by fostering self-belief, resilience and emotional literacy alongside academic achievement. Central to this is our therapeutic thinking approach, underpinned by the values of RESILIENCE, RESPECT and RESPONSIBILITY, which guide all interactions, behaviours and outcomes within our school community.
We explicitly develop oracy skills across the curriculum, enabling students to communicate confidently, articulate their thoughts, listen actively and engage respectfully with others. This supports both academic success and positive social relationships, equipping students with essential life skills.
Our curriculum is ambitious, inclusive and tailored to individual need. For Key Stage 3 pupils, the intention is successful reintegration into mainstream education through targeted academic, social and emotional support. For Key Stage 4 pupils, we provide personalised pathways aligned with the National Curriculum, focused on closing knowledge gaps and securing appropriate qualifications. All pupils are prepared to move confidently into education, employment or training, with the skills, attitudes and adaptability required to succeed in a rapidly changing world.
Implementation
Our bespoke curriculum is broad, balanced and personalised, designed to meet the diverse and often complex needs of our learners. It integrates academic learning with therapeutic thinking approaches, ensuring that emotional regulation, behaviour and readiness to learn are addressed alongside subject knowledge.
Teaching staff are calm, consistent and highly skilled in relational practice. They model positive behaviours, explicitly teach self-regulation strategies and use restorative approaches to support pupils in understanding and managing their actions. This creates a safe and purposeful learning environment where pupils feel valued and ready to learn.
Oracy is embedded across all subjects, with structured opportunities for discussion, debate, reflection and collaborative learning. Staff explicitly teach speaking and listening skills to strengthen pupils’ confidence, comprehension and ability to express themselves effectively.
Lessons are carefully adapted to meet individual needs, reducing barriers to learning. Assessment is used effectively to identify gaps in knowledge and inform personalised planning. Pupils are supported through:
A rigorous and supportive reintegration process is in place for pupils returning to mainstream education. This includes close collaboration with schools and families, clear communication of strategies and progress, and personalised transition plans. Pupils are supported through visits, reflection and ongoing review, ensuring they are equipped to succeed and sustain their placement.

Impact
Pupils at Harbour Vale School make meaningful progress academically, socially and emotionally from their individual starting points. They gain relevant qualifications, develop strong literacy and numeracy skills, and acquire the knowledge needed for their next steps.
Through our emphasis on therapeutic thinking and relational practice, pupils demonstrate improved self-regulation, resilience and behaviour for learning. They develop a secure understanding of how their actions affect themselves and others, enabling them to make positive choices.
Our focus on oracy ensures that pupils leave Harbour Vale able to communicate effectively, express their views with confidence and engage positively in a range of situations.

Child Development
Curriculum Intent
At Harbour Vale School, the Pearson BTEC Tech Award in Child Development is designed to inspire students to develop a secure understanding of child growth, development, and care from birth to five years. The curriculum aims to equip learners with practical knowledge, transferable skills, and an appreciation of the factors that influence children’s development, preparing them for further study and future careers within childcare, health, education, and related sectors.
Curriculum Implementation
At Harbour Vale School, the Child Development curriculum is delivered through a blend of theoretical learning and practical application, closely aligned to the Pearson BTEC Tech Award specification. Students investigate developmental milestones, health and wellbeing, play activities, and the factors affecting children’s development through engaging lessons, research, discussion, case studies, and vocationally relevant assignments. A range of assessment opportunities, retrieval activities, and practical tasks support students in developing their understanding and applying their knowledge to realistic scenarios. Learning is regularly monitored through formative assessment, knowledge checks, practice examination questions, and feedback that enables students to identify strengths and areas for development.
Curriculum Impact
Through studying Child Development at Harbour Vale School, students gain a strong understanding of how children grow, learn, and develop during their early years. They build confidence in applying their knowledge, develop valuable analytical and communication skills, and achieve success in both internal and external assessments. Students are assessed through a combination of internally assessed coursework components and an externally assessed examination, reflecting the vocational nature of the qualification and ensuring they can demonstrate both practical application and theoretical understanding. Students leave the course well prepared for progression to further education, apprenticeships, or careers in childcare, health, and education, with a clear understanding of the importance of promoting positive outcomes for young children.

Ethics and Philosophy
Intent Statement Teaching Ethics and Philosophy (AQA Religious Studies Short Course) to all Key Stage 3 and Key Stage 4 students fosters an understanding of diverse religious beliefs and practices, promotes critical thinking, and encourages respect for different perspectives. We aim to equip students with the skills to engage thoughtfully with moral and ethical issues, enhancing their personal development and preparing them for life in a multicultural society.
Implementation Statement The AQA Religious Studies Short Course will be implemented in Ethics and Philosophy lessons through a structured curriculum that includes a variety of teaching methods such as interactive discussions, analysing evidence, and looking at multimedia resources. Lessons will cover key themes such as beliefs, practices, and ethical issues in major world religions, with a focus on Christianity and Islam. Assessment will be conducted through a combination of self-review, peer-to-peer assessments and more formal written assignments, ensuring that students can demonstrate their understanding and analytical skills.
Impact Statement The impact of the AQA Religious Studies Short Course in Ethics and Philosophy lessons will be measured through student engagement, academic performance, and the development of critical thinking skills. Students will leave the course with a deeper appreciation for religious diversity, improved ability to articulate their views on ethical issues, and enhanced empathy towards others. Long-term, we expect students to apply their learning in real-world contexts, contributing positively to their communities and fostering a more inclusive society.

The Right of Withdrawal from RE
Harbour Vale School wishes to be an inclusive community but recognises the legal right of parents/carers to withdraw their child from Religious Education. However, the right of withdrawal does not extend to other areas of the curriculum when, as may happen on occasions, spontaneous questions on religious matters are raised by students or there are issues related to religion that arise in other subjects such as history or citizenship. We would urge any parents/carers considering this to contact the head teacher in the first instance to discuss any concerns.
